routes.label: Cancel factorials and complete the square

question: A positive integer \(n\) satisfies the equation \((n+1)!+(n+2)!=440\cdot n!.\) What is the sum of the digits of \(n?\)
solution:
All the factorials contain the factor \(n!\), which is nonzero. Using \((n+1)!=(n+1)n!\) and \((n+2)!=(n+2)(n+1)n!\), divide by \(n!\) to obtain
\[
(n+1)+(n+2)(n+1)=440.
\]
Expanding gives
\[
n^2+4n+3=440.
\]
Adding \(1\) to both sides completes the square:
\[
n^2+4n+4=441,
\qquad (n+2)^2=21^2.
\]
Since \(n\) is positive, \(n+2>0\), so \(n+2=21\) and \(n=19\). Its digit sum is \(1+9=\boxed{10}\), choice \(\text{C}\).
